Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz, Omar Rahman, Priya Singh (Astra Nova)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we only have 52 minutes so we'll try to be tight, quick go-round on current numbers then evan will walk through the new routing sims.
[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: sounds good, thanks. we've got Priya and Omar on in case we need platform or product decisions.
[00:18] Omar: yep, thanks.
[00:22] Evan: cool, i'll kick off with the CSV results we posted earlier, quick reminder incase folks didn't dig in — these are per-sequence percentiles over the last 48 hours from our lab, workload set A (conversation/summary mix). baseline is IncumbentAI's hosted endpoint using g4x equivalents.
[00:40] Evan: 50th median is basically comparable, 95th is about +18 ms for us, 99th is +42 ms, however when you enable our prefix KV cache for repeated convo tokens that 99th drops to +12ms.
[00:57] Dr. Lena Ortiz: wait can you say that again, the kv cache piece?
[01:02] Evan: yep, so kv cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) — for repeated prefixes we already maintain the key/value cache in memory, so subsequent calls that reuse prefix see much lower token generation latency. on your dataset about 60% of calls had a strong reuse pattern so it helps a lot.
[01:21] Priya: is that something we have to integrate or it is on your side?
[01:25] Evan: it's in the runtime, but you need to pin the session policy and set the cache window in the route config. i can send a sample route file.
[01:34] Maya: quick Q on cost, Priya asked last call about delta vs incumbent — we've given a rough per-token delta but the interesting bit is unit economics at scale.
[01:44] Priya: right, 1) latency within SLO, 2) cost per 1k tokens, 3) reliability.
[01:50] Evan: we ran two configs, hosted default (our stock quant profile) and a quantized int8 fast path. Hosted default was slightly cheaper than incumbent on median but slightly higher on 99th because of batching differences. int8 reduces unit compute by ~28% in lab but increases variance a little — we've seen some tokens jump more on tail occasionally.
[02:12] Omar: that's interesting, do you have numbers for sustained throughput? we're trying to push 300 rps steady and have bursts to 800 for promos.
[02:20] Evan: yes, sustained 300 rps typical sequence length 150 tokens — we measure throughput at 290 rps with 95th latency ~220ms for single shard dedicated slot. For bursts to 800 we recommend dedicated slot + autoscale bursts or fallback to cheaper region. We showed a routing playbook where requests over 700 switch to a warm pool with slightly lower precision model to keep tails in check.
[02:47] Dr. Lena Ortiz: so that's the fallback model you're calling the "compatible variant"? sometimes the transcript calls it comp variant.
[02:53] Evan: yes comp variant, lower context window but much cheaper and predictable. we can tune rollouts to keep fidelity high.
[03:00] Maya: can you explain a bit about the dedicated slot pricing? Priya asked how monthly committed capacity compares to on-demand.
[03:07] Evan: committed dedicated slot gives you predictable throughput (we can size for your 300 rps plus headroom) and saves cost at scale. On-demand has slightly higher per-token cost but you avoid commit. I'll put a delta sheet in the notes.
[03:18] Priya: we also need SSO and audit logs — SOC2 is table stakes, and we need to know what lives in our VPC.
[03:25] Maya: yes we've got Redwood Private options, SOC2, SAML/SSO and audit logs are all supported. for Private deployments we can push the control plane into your VPC, and keys integrate with your KMS.
[03:37] Priya: ok good. can you send the security deck again?
[03:39] Maya: will do after the call.
[03:41] [00:04] Evan: jumping back to the numbers, we purposely collected 1k request sample traces you asked for — subset A and subset B. Subset B has more long tails and that's where we see the 99th delta more pronounced.
[03:56] Evan: wanted to call out measurement caveats: our lab env matches your instance types but network variance in your colo can shift tail behavior, so that's why we recommend running a short head-to-head with your traces.
[04:09] Omar: can Redwood run the head-to-head here or we need to spin up a dedicated slot?
[04:13] Evan: we can run a lab head-to-head if you provide traces; it'll approximate but won't capture your infra egress NAT behavior. for true apples-to-apples we provision a short-lived dedicated slot in your account or a Private deployment sandbox.
[04:25] Dr. Lena Ortiz: timeline wise we want final vendor decision in mid-July, so we need two more weeks of tuned runs.
[04:32] Maya: that aligns. next two steps: evan run the int8 routing sims; lena upload traces; maya share pricing.
[04:40] [00:05] Priya: one more thing — error rates matter. we saw a slight uptick with quantize in your earlier tests, was that expected?
[04:48] Evan: yeah quantize can change numeric stability, especially on some attention kernels. we added a micro-tune per-layer and it reduced the error rate but not eliminated it. we'll run a sweep on your model family to identify the safest quant knobs.
[05:03] Dr. Lena Ortiz: can you also include a qualitative eval run — top 50 prompts — to make sure the output drift is negligible?
[05:10] Evan: absolutely, good ask. we'll attach the eval set and flag any regressions >3% on your metrics.
[05:16] [00:06] Maya: we also wanted to discuss routing thresholds — does Astra Nova want aggressive fallback to keep tail low or keep fidelity and accept higher tail?
[05:25] Priya: fidelity first, tail second, but we need predictable SLOs. so prefer smaller fidelity changes for fallback.
[05:32] Evan: okay we'll bias toward smaller model variants for fallback and tune threshold at 85th pct to start.
[05:38] Omar: on the infra notes - if we go with private, how much time to spin-up sandbox?
[05:44] Maya: for Private in your VPC we can do a sandbox in 7-10 business days, less if you accept a managed VPN. Dedicated slot in Redwood hosted is immediate once procured.
[05:54] [00:08] Priya: procurement question — will contract include SLAs for 99th latency?
[05:59] Maya: for Dedicated we can put latency SLOs in contract, for hosted we have standard SLOs and credits for breaches. we'll surface exact wording.
[06:07] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about data retention on logs — default is 30 days right? we might need 90 for audit.
[06:12] Evan: default is 30 but enterprise packages can extend to 90 or 365 for audit trails; you can also stream logs to your SIEM.
[06:19] [00:10] Evan: returning to the numbers slide — i want to call out unit-cost model: on the median our per-1k-token cost is ~0.88x of incumbent; at 99th due to variance it's ~1.12x unless you enable cache and routing. after cache+int8 that shifts to ~0.72x.
[06:37] Priya: that 0.72x with int8 is compelling but we need the eval on the top 50 prompts first.
[06:43] Maya: noted.
[06:45] [00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: small nit — earlier in the CSV I saw one line with very high latency and it correlated to a spike in token length, did you see that too?
[06:54] Evan: yes sequence length 1200 in that trace caused long KV lookups and kernel path change, that will blow tails. we recommend truncation policies for guardrails or split requests.
[07:06] Omar: can Redwood automatically enforce a truncation policy?
[07:09] Evan: yes route config can set max context and auto-truncate or reject. we generally prefer explicit client-side truncation to avoid surprises.
[07:16] [00:14] Maya: ok let's talk about the head-to-head we're going to run: Evan, you'll run the int8 + cache + routing config on our traces and post a per-sequence percentile CSV, Lena will validate with her team and we'll reconvene. anyone object?
[07:29] Priya: no objections.
[07:31] Evan: just to be clear — i'll post median, 95th, 99th, P99.9 and throughput numbers plus a short notes column with config used.
[07:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: do you capture RMS or variance? we care about jitter for user experience.
[07:44] Evan: yes we'll include stddev and p50-p99 ranges.
[07:47] [00:16] Maya: timeline recap — Evan posts by Friday, Lena uploads traces by Monday, Maya posts pricing by Friday. deep-dive scheduled next week.
[07:58] Omar: small question on fallback models, do you keep them warm? warm pool sizing?
[08:03] Evan: yes warm pool is sized independently, we recommend 20% warm for your burst profile, warms are cheaper because KV is seeded but they do cost.
[08:11] Priya: will warm pool increase cost substantially?
[08:14] Evan: modestly, maybe +7-12% on steady-state cost depending on size.
[08:20] [00:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: procurement wise we might ask for a 30 day trial in our environment before commit, is that doable?
[08:27] Maya: yes we can offer a short pilot in your VPC or a managed sandbox, terms to be discussed.
[08:33] Priya: one last security Q — is there an option for HSM key storage for model keys?
[08:38] Evan: yes we support KMS and HSM integration for Private deployments.
[08:42] [00:20] Maya: ok wrapping up the technical bits — Evan any blockers on running the head-to-head?
[08:48] Evan: only need traces and a small allowlist of request types; i also want to validate whether your tokenization differs (some of your pre-processing appears to split emojis differently).
[08:59] Dr. Lena Ortiz: good catch, we'll include a note.
[09:02] [00:22] Evan: also note that our int8 path is model-family specific — for a few of your custom layers we may fallback to mixed precision for stability, that's fine but changes the math.
[09:12] Priya: okay as long as you document when mixed precision was used.
[09:17] [00:23] Maya: commercial ask — if we go dedicated, can we get a price hold for 6 months?
[09:22] Evan: yes we can do a price hold as part of a reserved capacity agreement.
[09:25] [00:24] Dr. Lena Ortiz: do you have reference customers in healthcare — we have compliance concerns.
[09:30] Maya: yes we can introduce you to two references; both used Redwood Dedicated + Private for PHI workloads.
[09:36] Omar: great.
[09:38] [00:26] Evan: one more technical tangent — we saw at 800 rps the incumbent used a different kernel that batched across multiple requests and produced lower median but worse 99th. our approach tries to keep tails bounded with per-request batching heuristics.
[09:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: can you share the kernel selection notes?
[09:55] Evan: i'll paste a short note and the kernel mapping we used.
[09:59] [00:28] Priya: sounds good.
[10:01] Maya: any other blockers?
[10:03] Omar: none.
[10:05] [00:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: final ask — when you send the per-sequence CSV can you flag any cases with token length > 1k and annotate whether truncation policy applied?
[10:12] Evan: yes will do.
[10:14] [00:31] Maya: perfect. we'll reconvene after runs — propose Tue 2027-06-29 14:00 UTC for deep-dive, does that work?
[10:22] Priya: works for me.
[10:24] Dr. Lena Ortiz: yep works.
[10:26] Evan: ok i'll set up the meeting and include an infra deep slide deck.
[10:30] [00:34] Maya: quick recap for notes: send security deck, pricing delta, int8 routing run, traces uploaded, schedule deep-dive.
[10:40] Priya: thanks everyone.
[10:42] [00:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks.
[10:44] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.
